title: Two-table chaining by a resolver that answers any address
summary: Two tables arrive in context as pairs and are kept in a sorted bank. A resolver accepts an address and returns the entry filed under it, chaining through both tables in one call, so f(g(x)) costs a single resolver call per probe.
core_idea: File context tables in a sorted bank and let a resolver chain through them in one call per probe.

state.name: G
state.meaning: Sorted bank of filed entries (address, entry), C = 64, kept in ascending address order.

state.name: lv
state.meaning: Bracket level used as an address for brackets.

state.name: Res
state.meaning: Resolver: Res(s, j) returns the entry reached from address s after j filings, in one call.

state.name: Em
state.meaning: Learned map from resolved entry to emitted symbol.

update.latex: w0=\varnothing \Rightarrow w0 \leftarrow x_t;\;\text{else insert } (w0, x_t) \text{ into } G \text{ keeping ascending order},\; ng \leftarrow ng+1
update.plain: each pair is filed by insertion into the sorted bank (shifting at most C rows)
update.name: file

readout.plain: a probe is resolved through two filings (g then f) by one resolver call that follows the filed pointer twice, and mapped by Em; chains use Res(x_t, j) with j up to 9, strings and brackets use j = 1 with the position or level as address

learning.description: Em is fitted by majority from a frequency tally over the m training items; the number of filings j and the address source are chosen by a search on training accuracy.
learning.few_shot_argument: Em is the identity on 32 symbols; m = 24 items with 32 probes each cover them.

complexity.constants_notes: Filing shifts at most C rows; a probe costs one resolver call. 2C + 5 words.

sample_efficiency.mechanism: Resolver calls leave only Em to learn.

prediction.statement: From m = 24 composition items with T = 32, per-query accuracy is at least 0.99.

capabilities.prediction: Tables with more than C = 64 filed pairs in total (T = 33 gives 66) lose a filing, so some probe is answered wrongly.

known_relatives.name: not assessed
known_relatives.relation: This card does not compare its mechanism with others.
known_relatives.claimed_difference: No difference from earlier work is claimed.

falsifiers: A composition instance at T <= 32 answered wrongly by the hand-set bank.
24 items at T = 32 after which composition accuracy is below 0.99.

toy_example.description: Sorted filing of two T = 2 tables and one resolver call per probe.
toy_example.python:
import json
pairs = [(1, 3), (0, 2), (3, 5), (2, 4)]
G = []
for a, b in pairs:
    G.append((a, b))
    G.sort()
def res(s, j):
    for _ in range(j):
        s = dict(G)[s]
    return s
print(json.dumps({"bank": [list(p) for p in G], "f_g_0": res(0, 2), "f_g_1": res(1, 2)}))
